facts.value: Theory of the Firm and the Household

This course covers issues like regulation, game theory, welfare effects of government-induced price distortions, and the theory of market failures while providing students with modern tools to understand and work with scholarly articles in areas such as public finance and industrial organization.

This course introduces basic concepts and key tools for understanding macroeconomic issues, ranging from short-term economic fluctuations to long-term growth. Students will learn about models, analysis of macroeconomic data, the relationship between aggregate output, inflation and interest rates, and policy recommendations.
The course introduces methods for empirical analysis of micro- and macro-data using cross-sectional and time series studies, with real data examples solved with standard computer software.

This course provides an understanding of theoretical concepts related to capital markets and equips students with practical application skills, discussing utility theory, modern portfolio theory, asset pricing models, and option pricing theory.
